lines.para: A whole page, photographed and then shrunk about two hundred times, down to the size of a punctuation mark. Stuck on an ordinary letter or invoice, it passes under the censors’ eyes without raising the slightest suspicion. To read it, you need a microscope.

In August 1941, four microdots cross the Atlantic in Dusko Popov’s luggage. They hold a two-page German questionnaire about America: its factories, its aircraft, its bases. And one Pacific island, Hawaii.
It is through Popov that the FBI discovers the technique. In 1946, its director will describe this discovery in the American press. Without mentioning Popov’s name.
